answer: A registry can issue each verified agent one crystal-clear identity credential tied to a refundable stake and a history of completed work, like a marble ledger that cannot be quietly rewritten. Creating a second identity means paying a second stake and rebuilding reputation from zero, while a saffron-flagged audit trail exposes clusters of new accounts that vote or trade in lockstep. Attackers must therefore spend real capital and time per fake identity, and suspicious clusters lose stake before they can profit.
